[[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] in red & [[Green Party of England and Wales |Green Party]] in green. | title = council control | posttitle = Subsequent council control | before_election = | before_party = Labour Party (UK) | after_election = | after_party = Labour Party (UK) }} The '''2022 Newham London Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022. All 66 members of [[Newham London Borough Council]] were elected. The election took place alongside [[2022 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]] and [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|elections to local authorities across the United Kingdom]]. In the [[2018 Newham London Borough Council election|previous 2018 local election]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] maintained its control of the council, winning all 60 seats. The 2022 election took place under new election boundaries, which increased the number of councillors to 66. The election coincided with an election for the [[mayor of Newham]] after a governance referendum resulted in the borough keeping a [[Directly elected mayors in England and Wales|directly elected mayor]]. In the 2022 local election, the Labour Party won all but two seats, which went to the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]], for the ward of Stratford Olympic Park. ==Background== A total of 253 candidates stood in the election for the 66 seats being contested across 24 wards. Candidates included a full slate from the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] (as had been the case at every election since the borough council had been formed in 1964), and a full slate from the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] for the first time. The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] stood 65 candidates (not a full slate of 66, due to a delayed Election Officer's ruling of an over-subscribed nomination), making it the first time since 2010 they have not stood a full slate. Other candidates who ran were 26 Christian Peoples Alliance, 17 Liberal Democrats, 4 TUSC, 3 Reform UK, and 6 Independents.{{cite web |title=LE2022 SOPN |url=https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/u/1/d/1qY6r_FU4k8LoPStSGEBqIyO2SCwChtX9b0Q6sD5n6h0/htmlview# |website=Google Drive |publisher=Election Maps UK |access-date=11 April 2022}} ===History=== [[File:Newham Ward Map 2022.png|thumb|New ward boundaries for the London Borough of Newham 2022]] The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police and fire.{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}} Newham has been under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control since its creation, besides a period of [[no overall control]] from 1968 to 1971. In the [[2018 Newham London Borough Council election|most recent election in 2018]], Labour won all sixty seats with 67.2% of the vote across the borough. The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] received 15.2% of the vote, the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] received 5.9% of the vote and the [[Green Party of England and Wales]] received 5.2% of the vote but none of these won any seats.{{Cite web|last=Grafton-Green|first=Chloe Chaplain, Patrick|date=2018-05-05|title=The full list of results for London's local Labour candidate [[Rokhsana Fiaz]] became [[mayor of Newham]] in the concurrent mayoral election, succeeding [[Robin Wales]] with 73.4% of the vote in the first round.{{Cite web|title=Rokhsana Fiaz, London's first directly elected woman mayor|url=https://muslimnews.co.uk/newspaper/home-news/rokhsana-fiaz-londons-first-directly-elected-woman-mayor/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=The Muslim News}} ===Council term=== In September 2018, Veronica Oakeshott, a Labour candidate for Boleyn ward, resigned because she was moving to Oxfordshire.{{Cite by-election|url=https://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/boleyn-by-election-won-by-labour-candidate-after-resignation-of-3193732|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Newham Recorder|language=en-UK}} In August 2020, Julianne Marriot, a Labour councillor for East Ham Central, resigned for work reasons.{{Cite web|last=Brookes|first=Andrew|date=2020-08-05|title=East Ham Central ward councillor resigns|url=https://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/local-council/councillor-julianne-marriott-stands-down-3263588|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Newham Recorder|language=en-UK}} Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], a by-election to fill her seat could not be held until 6 May 2021 alongside the [[2021 London mayoral election]] and [[2021 London Assembly election|London Assembly election]]. The Labour candidate Farah Nazeer was elected, with the Conservative candidate coming in second place.{{Cite web|last=Boyle|first=Caislin|date=2021-05-10|title=East Ham Central welcomes new Labour councillor|url=https://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/labour-wins-east-ham-central-by-election-7959118|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Newham Recorder|language=en-UK}} In July 2020, eighteen councillors submitted a complaint to the Labour Party about the mayor [[Rokhsana Fiaz]], claiming she treated people unfairly, humiliated them and "picked on colleagues". Two councillors also complained that she hadn't dealt with antisemitism in the local party. After she was re-selected as the Labour mayoral candidate, with the party having responded to neither complaint, Pat Murphy and Quintin Peppiatt resigned from the Labour group.{{Cite web |last=Cox |first=Michael |date=2022-03-01 |title=Formal complaint lodged against Newham mayor with allegations of 'unfair treatment' |url=https://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/newham-councillors-make-rokhsana-fiaz-complaint-8715884 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=Newham Recorder |language=en-UK}} As with most London boroughs, Newham elected its councillors under new boundaries decided by the [[Local Government Boundary Commission for England]], which it produced after a period of consultation. The number of councillors increased from 60 to 66, under new boundaries with eighteen three-councillor wards and six two-councillor wards.{{Cite web|last=Cox|first=Sophie|date=2020-11-18|title=Six extra councillors set for Newham as final ward boundary recommendations published|url=https://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/local-council/newham-ward-boundary-final-recommendations-6551232|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Newham Recorder|language=en-UK}}{{cite referendum=== A referendum was held on 6 May 2021 on whether to retain the mayoral system, where voters elect a mayor every four years, who appoints their own cabinet, or to change to the committee system, where councillors select members of committees and a council leader.{{Cite web|last=King|first=Jonathan|date=2021-04-28|title=Newham's governance referendum: the case for both options|url=https://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/newham-governance-referendum-explained-7927720|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Newham Recorder|language=en-UK}} The result was to retain the mayoral system, with 56% of voters supporting the status quo.{{Cite web|last=King|first=Jonathan|date=2021-05-10|title=Mayor pledges to continue focus on election promises after Newham referendum result|url=https://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/newham-referendum-result-keeps-directly-elected-mayor-7960128|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Newham Recorder|language=en-UK}} ===Changes since 2022=== 7 October 2021 |option1 = Elected mayor |yes = 45,960 |yespct = 55.8 |option2 = Committee system |no = 36,424 |nopct = 44.2 |majorityneeded = |valid = |validpct = |invalid = |invalidpct = |total = 85,087 |turnoutpct = 38 |turnoutneeded = |electorate = |source = }} ==Electoral process== Newham, like other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years. The previous election took place in 2018. The election took place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors had as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected. All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over were entitled to vote in the election. People who live at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, were entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}} Voting in-person at polling stations took place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters were able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election. ==Council composition== File:Newham 2021.svg|{{centre|Council composition after the 2018 election}} File:Newham council May 2022 with its indie councillors.png|{{centre|Council composition ahead of the 2022 election}} File:Newham Council 2022.svg|{{centre|Council composition after the 2022 election}} {| class="wikitable" |- ! colspan="3" | After 2018 election ! colspan="3" | After 2022 election |- ! colspan="2" | Party !
